purpose: Test whether a foreground-only OpenPose T2I-Adapter can add the low bent ticket pose to an SDXL identity LoRA without reintroducing full-frame Canny interference.

runtime_preflight.result: PNG saved with sequential CPU offload

pose_input.detector: controlnet_aux OpenPose body map without face or hand landmarks

assessment.0.0: The LoRA baseline produced a front full-body woman with partial clothing and bag cues, but did not perform the bent ticket action or preserve the diagonal strap.
assessment.0.35: The character remained upright while the jacket/trouser structure drifted; the requested bend and ticket contact did not appear.
assessment.0.7: The result changed to a rear view with a large backpack, losing the face, navy flap bag, and diagonal strap while still not reproducing the target action.
assessment.conclusion: The adapter is feasible on 8 GB but this foreground-only raw OpenPose map and SDXL identity LoRA do not jointly pass pose or identity. Do not combine this branch with scene Canny or run a finer scale sweep. Investigate reference-conditioned pose-transfer methods instead.

retention: Only this review record is retained. Preflight and scale-sweep PNGs, materialized dataset, regenerated LoRA adapter, and experimental scripts were removed after review.
